agree.reason: Marisol gets a believable need, a modest target she can check, and a direct admission of the late report with a fix, so she will probably recommend it, though she may still ask about running costs and cold storage at the site.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's unsupported 'double fresh food' claim, keeps every number true to the brief, and says the possible extra gains are not counted; the only stretch is calling 9,000 pounds a 'floor'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out a 50% increase over the three harvest months (18,000 to 27,000 pounds) and about 12% for the year, and it states the reserve left after the purchase, though it never calculates cost per pound or per household.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated as the facts show it: without a van the food bank keeps turning down about 9,000 pounds of farm produce each summer, set against its current baseline of about 6,000 pounds a month.

qualification.reason: The 9,000-pound target and monthly tracking give Marisol a number to check, but there is no reporting date and nothing says what happens if the target or a deadline is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the late-report concern, the drop in reserves and the question of who will drive, but leaves out fuel, insurance and maintenance, and what happens to cold food after it reaches the building.

fit.reason: It is a sectioned grant narrative that appears to come in under the 500-word limit.
